description: Mutation sweep over the burned/fresh split in the signature inventory. Written because this module's untested guard is the one that actually stopped something: three days of B11a collection completed, produced a clean 33,866-member cohort, and stage 4 refused it in one second against EXPECTED_MEMBERS = 1601, a constant describing the B9 study. No test in the suite mentioned that constant. Every mutant here is a way the replacement could be wrong in the same silent style -- a mode that never selects fresh, a pin that still applies, a survivor of the old one-message-two-conditions ambiguity, or a fresh path that quietly falls back to the burned horizon.

expected_survivors.name: the selection is relaxed to a subset test, which every cherry-pick passes
expected_survivors.why: EQUIVALENT UNDER THE CHECK ABOVE IT, and I only learned that by trying to kill it. `assert_subsample` refuses first when the declared N differs from the member count, so by the time the selection is compared, |present| == n. `expected` is exactly the n smallest keys, so |present| == |expected|, and a subset of equal size IS equality -- present <= expected and present == expected cannot differ for any artifact that reaches this line. I wrote a strict-subset fixture expecting to kill it and it survived, because making the subset strict requires an inconsistent N, which the size guard rejects first. COUPLED, NOT INDEPENDENT: if the size check were ever removed or moved below this one, the equivalence dissolves and this mutant becomes killable immediately -- a subsample that drops curves would then pass a subset test. The sweep will say so, because this declaration will start failing.
